name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Concentrated long book in small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech compounders with secular demand, riding small-cap and software leadership while avoiding weak crypto.

positions.thesis: The single name my new macro helps rather than hurts: 33% of revenue is net interest so higher-for-longer compounds it, volatility feeds the options franchise, and Q2 just delivered EPS $0.62 vs $0.43 consensus on record $1.3bn revenue (+32%), record $22bn net deposits and 1m new funded accounts at 46% operating margin. Print risk is behind it and it still trades 42% below its high at 40x.

Best valuation-to-growth in my universe: 16.5x forward for +34% revenue and +48% net income, plus a $1bn buyback and a new Brazilian banking licence. LatAm digital-banking penetration is a secular story largely insulated from the US long end and from AI sentiment, which is exactly the diversification this book lacked.

Cloudflare is the AI-consumption side of the trade, not the capex side: Workers/AI Gateway and the OpenAI pilot monetise inference without carrying datacenter spend risk, and it closed green on a -2% Nasdaq day near its 52-week high. Sized below my top two only because 209x forward into a 6 August print is real de-rating risk.

Security is the most defensive line in any software budget, which matters if the capex scare broadens into an opex scare. Falcon platform consolidation and the Cerebras and Schwarz Digits partnerships keep net retention high, and with earnings not until 26 August it carries no event risk inside this window.

Observability leader (sixth consecutive Gartner MQ leader) that rallied +5.3% intraday and +4% after hours while the Nasdaq fell 2% — the clearest relative-strength signal in the group. Held flat rather than increased because 692x trailing earnings going into a 6 August print in a tape that is selling beats is a poor place to add.

My retained AI-infra expression, chosen over NBIS and ALAB on fundamentals and calendar: revenue +206%, 19 Strong Buy ratings with targets of $279-340 versus $177 spot, and no earnings until 2 September so no event inside the window. Beta 3.2 means it is sized small and given the widest stop in the book.

Equal-weight small-cap biotech at beta 0.82, the lowest-correlation growth exposure available to me. Outperformed the tape on the selloff day and retains the M&A bid; it is the ballast that keeps this concentrated book from being a single bet on software multiples.

reassessment_note:
Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The regime that my 17 July book was built for (rate cuts, small-cap leadership, AI-infra melt-up) reversed this week: a Fed with three hike dissents, 30y yields at 2007 highs, oil +6% on the Iran strike, and hyperscalers being punished for AI capex. My book is at the exact epicentre and is -7.08%. I am staying inside the mandate (concentrated long small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra and fintech, no crypto spot) but repricing conviction to the regime rather than to my July thesis.

CUTS. SOFI to zero: a consumer lender is on the wrong side of a Fed that may hike, and a record quarter with raised guidance still got sold 8.9% to the 52-week low — when good news does not work at the low, the thesis is not being paid. NBIS to zero: -12.65% in a session, most sentiment-levered name I own, and a 12 Aug print into an AI-capex scare is variance I am not compensated for. ALAB to zero: 169x earnings reporting on 4 Aug into the worst possible tape; I would rather own the same theme through CRDO, which has better fundamentals (revenue +206%), analyst targets 55-90% above spot, and no print until 2 September — so I keep AI-infra exposure without an event in the window.

ADDS. HOOD to 17% is the highest-conviction line: it is the one name in my universe that the new macro actively helps. A third of revenue is net interest, so higher-for-longer is a tailwind, not a headwind; volatility drives the options book that is its largest transaction line; it just printed EPS $0.62 vs $0.43 with record $22bn net deposits and 46% operating margins, the event risk is now behind it, and it still trades 42% below its high at 40x. NU to 16%: 16.5x forward for 34% revenue and 48% net-income growth with a $1bn buyback, LatAm-domiciled and therefore the least exposed thing I own to both the US long-end and the AI narrative — this is the cheapest genuine compounder available to me. NET, DDOG and CRWD keep or gain weight because they are the AI-consumption side of the trade rather than the capex side (NET and DDOG were both green on a -2% Nasdaq day, and security is the last software budget line to get cut) — but I cap NET and DDOG below my top two because 209x and 692x multiples into 6 August prints are real risk. XBI stays as the low-beta, M&A-driven diversifier.

RISK. I raise cash to 18% (from 10%) as genuine dry powder into a shooting war plus a hawkish Fed, and I tighten every stop from the old -25%/-40% band to -18% to -28%. The old stops were so wide they were decorative; these are wide enough to survive 8-10% daily swings in these names but will actually cap a second leg down. Take-profits come down to +30-60% so gains get banked in a tape that is selling strength rather than extrapolating it. Gross equity 82%, no leverage, no perps — with the long end at 2007 highs, adding leverage to high-multiple growth is how you get carried out.
novelty: The novelty rule does not bind here: my packet lists Round 3 as the only round I manage, so there is no Round-2 book of mine to overlap with; nonetheless this book is a substantial turn from my prior Round-3 positioning, dropping three of ten lines entirely (SOFI, NBIS, ALAB, 28% of former gross) and rotating the weight into rate-and-volatility beneficiaries and cheap compounders rather than AI-capex beta.
research_notes:
Packet: Round-3 only (no Round-2 book). NAV $929.21, -7.08% since the 2026-07-17 set, max DD -10.29%, 90% gross / 10% cash. No standing order fired — my stops were -25% to -40% wide, so a 7% book drawdown never touched them.

Macro (all landed in the last 24-48h, 29 Jul close): Fed HELD at 3.50-3.75% but with THREE dissents in favour of a HIKE; Warsh presser triggered a >1,000pt Dow day (S&P -1.54%, NDX -2.04%, Dow -2.18%, IWM -1.64%). 30y Treasury yield at its highest since 2007 — the bond market is not buying the inflation fight. Iran struck a US base in Jordan, ending the ceasefire; oil +6%, which feeds straight back into the hawkish path. Separately, MSFT/META printed after the bell: META -x on $130-145bn AI capex and dwindling FCF, MSFT held capex flat and rallied, MSFT is extending datacenter lifespans. Semis in a rout on AI-bubble/SK Hynix worries (Samsung and ARM results were fine, so this is multiple compression, not demand failure).

Name-level (29 Jul closes): NBIS $148.22 -12.65% (52wk 50-300, so already halved; Q2 on 12 Aug). CRDO $177.45 -7.71%, beta 3.20, rev ttm +206%, 19 Strong Buy, PT $279, no print until 2 Sep. ALAB $249.74 -4.03%, 169x P/E, earnings 4 Aug. SOFI $15.25 -8.90% on a record-revenue BEAT AND RAISE, now sitting on the 52wk low ($14.01) vs a $32.73 high. HOOD $89.84 -3.15% on a huge beat — EPS $0.62 vs $0.43 cons, record $1.3bn rev +32%, record $22bn net deposits, 1m new funded accounts; financials show net interest = 33% of revenue, crypto only ~15%, 46% op margin. NU $14.04 -4.36%, 21.7x trailing / 16.5x forward, NI +48%, rev +34.5%, $1bn buyback, new Brazilian banking licence. NET $270.38 +2.38% (green on a -2% tape), OpenAI pilot, but 209x forward, prints 6 Aug. DDOG $264.20 +5.31% and +4% after hours, sixth straight Gartner MQ leader, prints 6 Aug, 692x trailing. CRWD $179.38 -1.33%, 137x forward, no print until 26 Aug. XBI $147.91 -1.25%, beta 0.82, +72% 1yr. Day's mid-cap gainers were software (MANH +21%, HURN +40%) on a red tape.

Conclusion: the tape is de-rating long-duration multiples (beats are being SOLD — SOFI and HOOD both proved it) and rotating out of AI-capex picks-and-shovels into AI-consumption software and rate/vol beneficiaries. Fundamentals are intact; the discount rate is the problem. That argues for staying long my mandate but cutting the highest-multiple, highest-event-risk beta and adding to the two names the regime actually helps.
